scenes.title: Lift Slightly and Open Wide
scenes.summary: At ten sharp on Festival Saturday, fifty smiling visitors stream beneath the cream-and-gold pennants past the gleaming oval founding plaque.
scenes.intro: Ten chimes echo cheerfully across {CITY} as both iron gates of {SHOW} swing wide open onto sunlit {STREET}. {M2}, {F1}, and {M1} stand beside the gleaming oval brass plaque greeting a steady stream of delighted festival visitors. Listen first.
story: M2
Good morning and welcome to {SHOW}—mind the threshold and enjoy the courtyard shade!
F1
Here is your festival map, madam—hot tea is left, and Room Nine is straight ahead!
M1
Watch how every third visitor pauses right here to read our polished oval brass plaque.
M2
Someone just took a photograph of our twenty cream-and-gold pennant flags overhead!
F1
And nobody had to crawl on hands and knees under a giant canvas teapot, {M2}!
M2
Team adaptation, {F1}—the hallmark of great hospitality management!
M1
Thirty visitors inside already, and nobody is crowding the walkway thanks to the east arcade.
F1
Look at the Clock-Square woodcarver beaming behind his display of hand-carved spoons!
M2
Inviting them in really made the whole courtyard feel twice as lively, did it not?
M1
Listen—{F3} and {M3} just struck the opening chord on the walnut piano!
F1
Every head in the courtyard just turned toward the open green shutters with a smile!
M2
Hold the gate post, {M1}, while {F1} and I check on {F2} at the pastry booth!
scenes.outro: Sunlight glints off brass and fluttering pennants as music draws fifty happy visitors deep into the courtyard! See you at the café booth next time.

scenes.title: Three Tiers Standing Proud
scenes.summary: At the bustling café booth, F2, M4, and F1 serve steaming mint tea and braided honey-fig twists from the rock-solid three-tier brass stand.
scenes.intro: At eleven under the gold-teapot sign, {F2} and {M4} pour fragrant mint tea into stoneware and borrowed porcelain cups as {F1} replenishes the gleaming three-tier brass stand. Let us listen in first.
story: F1
Twelve more braided honey-fig twists going onto the top and middle brass plates!
F2
Forty-eight twists gone in sixty minutes, and our three-tier stand has not budged once!
M4
Even the Clock-Square coordinator bought three twists and asked for your baker card, {F2}!
F2
Wait—those twelve porcelain teacups they lent us match our cream runners like a dream!
F1
Table four says the rosemary scent by the cedar screens makes the figs taste even sweeter!
M4
Tray five is five minutes from coming out of the oven—forty fresh twists ready!
F2
Listen to the archway: the flutes and violin just joined {F3} and {M3} at eleven!
F1
Oh, goosebumps—five instruments playing the Courtyard Waltz together in G major!
M4
Even people waiting in line for tea are swaying gently in time with the waltz!
F2
{F1}, carry two warm twists over to the musicians as soon as they take their bow!
M4
I have the teapot urns covered here, Chef—step out and hear the final verse!
F2
Best Saturday morning this kitchen has ever seen!
scenes.outro: Borrowed porcelain teacups and lock-washed brass shine side by side as five instruments fill the courtyard with waltz music! See you inside Room 9 next time.

scenes.title: Music Across the Stones
scenes.summary: As the five-piece Courtyard Waltz finishes to thunderous applause, F1 brings warm pastries into Room 9 for a glowing F3 and M3.
scenes.intro: Noon sunlight floods Room 9 as the final chord of the five-piece Courtyard Waltz rings out through the open green shutters to sustained cheering from sixty listeners outside. {F1} steps in carrying a plate of warm twists for {F3} and {M3}. Listen first.
story: F1
Listen to that applause echoing all the way down {STREET}, {F3} and {M3}!
F3
Those two young flute players lifted the melody right up into the branches of the tree!
M3
And did you hear how quiet the brick echo stayed even with sixty people standing outside?
F1
People in the very back row by the fountain heard every soft piano note clearly!
F3
Your four oatmeal-linen cedar screens passed the ultimate festival test, {M3}!
M3
Wait—two visitors from the Municipal Music School asked who designed our acoustic panels!
F1
NO WAY! Did you give them the card for your new studio four doors down {STREET}?!
M3
Handed them my card AND invited them to see our wooden joinery on Monday!
F3
Wonderful news, {M3}! Now eat a warm honey-fig twist before our one-thirty set!
F1
Look out under the shade tree: {M2} is giving a history tour around table one!
F3
With his reading glasses still on his nose at noon? Let us go witness history!
M3
Save half a twist for number ten and his violin—out to the shade tree!
scenes.outro: Sixty guests cheer the five-piece ensemble, {M3}'s new studio wins fans, and {M2} holds court under the shade tree! See you outside next time.

scenes.title: The Quiet Couple Returns
scenes.summary: Finishing a warm afternoon story about the third courtyard stone, M2 discovers that the quiet Tuesday couple in the back row are wearing official Festival Judge ribbons!
scenes.intro: At half past two under the courtyard shade tree, {M2} wraps up a cheerful five-minute history talk for a circle of visitors, then steps over beside {F3} and {M1} near the sunroom shutters. Let us listen in first.
story: M2
Zero boasting, zero white gloves—I simply told the honest story of Room Nine!
F3
Everyone loved hearing about the time capsule under stone number three, {M2}.
M1
You even gave credit to the bricklayers and the baker, boss; miracles happen.
M2
Wait a second... look beside cedar screen two at that polite couple holding teacups!
M1
Aha—the quiet retired couple who drank tea here on Tuesday afternoon while you hunted neckties!
F3
Look at the blue satin badges pinned to their lapels today, {M2}!
M2
OFFICIAL FESTIVAL JUDGES?! They visited us anonymously on Tuesday AND came back today?!
M1
Because on Tuesday nobody hovered over them with a brass metronome—they got real tea.
F3
Look, the lady just smiled and raised her teacup toward you and the Clock-Square table!
M2
Thank heavens I stayed upstairs looking for my necktie on Tuesday afternoon!
M1
Now keep smiling normally; {M4} walks up to City Hall at four for the closing ceremony.
F3
Prize or no prize, {M2}, look around these stones—your house already won the day.
scenes.outro: Tuesday's quiet tea drinkers turn out to be the real Festival Judges—and at five sharp {M4} returns from City Hall! See you next time.

scenes.title: The Velvet Box at Five
scenes.summary: At five in the afternoon, M4 returns from the Municipal Festival Stage carrying a blue velvet box—{SHOW} has unanimously won the Golden Courtyard Plaque!
scenes.intro: Warm five-sharp golden light slants across the courtyard as the afternoon crowds wind down into cosy neighbourly tables. Suddenly {M4} strides briskly through the arched gate holding a square navy-blue velvet box before {M2} and {F2}. Listen first.
story: M2
{M4}! Why are you walking so solemnly with a navy-blue velvet box in both hands?!
F2
Do not tease us for another second, {M4}—what happened at the Municipal Stage?!
M4
All three Festival Judges signed one unanimous citation for the {CITY} Golden Courtyard Plaque!
M2
Which courtyard won it, {M4}?! Tell me before my glasses leap back up my forehead!
M4
Lift the brass clasp yourself and read the engraved gold plate inside, {M2}!
M2
Awarded to {SHOW} on {STREET}—for Living Music, Artisan Bread, and an Open Gate!
F2
WE WON! {SHOW} WON THE GOLDEN COURTYARD PLAQUE ON OUR VERY FIRST TRY!
M4
Wait until you hear why all three judges voted unanimously, {M2}!
F2
Was it the cedar acoustic screens, or the walnut piano, or the honey-fig twists?!
M4
All three—PLUS welcoming Clock-Square Courtyard inside when their street pipe burst!
M2
Hear that, friends and neighbours?! Free cinnamon rolls and fresh tea for every table!
F2
Call {M1} and {F1} with the screwdriver—this golden plaque belongs on our gate!
scenes.outro: Living music, warm bread, and neighbourly generosity earn {SHOW} the unanimous Golden Courtyard Plaque! See you at the gate arch next time.

scenes.title: Opposite the Founding Brass
scenes.summary: At twilight inside the stone gate arch, M1 mounts the new Golden Courtyard Plaque directly opposite the century-old oval builder's plaque while F1 holds the spirit level.
scenes.intro: At half past six as golden twilight settles along {STREET}, {M1} and {F1} stand quietly inside the arched stone entrance fastening the shining new festival plaque opposite the old oval brass motto. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: F1
Bubble right in the centre of the glass, {M1}—tighten that last brass screw gently!
M1
Four turns to the right... solid as the stone arch itself, {F1}.
F1
Look at both plaques facing each other across the threshold: eighteen-ninety and today!
M1
Old brass on the left welcoming travellers in, new gold on the right thanking neighbours.
F1
Remember my very first Monday morning here when the front door handle stuck on me?
M1
You learned to lift the handle faster than anybody I ever trained at that desk.
F1
Wait—was that an actual official compliment from {M1} without a single grumble?!
M1
Do not let it go to your head; someone still has to balance the Saturday ledger.
F1
I will balance ten paper ledgers gladly—come look at the rooftop lanterns lighting up!
M1
Twenty-four coral and gold moons shining steady above a very tidy little courtyard.
F1
{F2} saved a plate of honey-fig twists at table one just for the seven of us!
M1
Tool pouch closed—let us go hear what {F3} is announcing under the tree.
scenes.outro: Old brass and new gold face each other across the open gate as twenty-four lanterns glow for our seven friends! See you under the tree next time.

scenes.title: Lessons Twice a Week
scenes.summary: Gathered around table one under the evening lanterns, F3 delights F2 and M3 with news that she is moving onto {STREET} permanently and teaching piano in Room 9 twice a week!
scenes.intro: At eight in the evening, the festival crowds have drifted happily home, leaving {SHOW} peaceful beneath its glowing balcony lanterns. Around table one under the shade tree, {F2} pours hot mint tea for {F3} and {M3}. Listen first.
story: F2
Raise your teacups to the finest chamber musicians and acoustic builders on {STREET}!
M3
And to the baker whose sixty honey-fig twists vanished before noon, {F2}!
F3
Before my fortnight in Room Four ends tomorrow, my dears, I have a confession.
F2
Oh no, {F3}—please do not tell us you are packing that blue suitcase on Sunday!
F3
Quite the opposite: I am only packing Room Four to move six doors down {STREET}!
M3
WAIT A SECOND! Did you rent that bright first-floor flat above the stationery shop?!
F3
Signed the papers yesterday morning—with morning sun AND zero stairs for groceries!
F2
You are becoming our real permanent neighbour right alongside the new studio?!
F3
Only on one condition: {M2} lets me teach piano in Room Nine on Tuesdays and Thursdays!
M3
Young piano students learning scales on a rescued walnut piano inside an acoustic sunroom!
F2
And every Friday at six, our whole crew still meets right here at table one!
F3
From one swapped suitcase at the station to finding home on {STREET} for good!
scenes.outro: Nobody has to say goodbye to {F3}—Room 9 gains afternoon piano students, and {STREET} gains a beloved neighbour for good! One final scene for Season 4!

scenes.title: The Old Bakehouse Arch
scenes.summary: Closing the front desk at nine-thirty Saturday night, F1, M2, and M1 read a note in the Festival Guest Book from a national guidebook editor asking about a forgotten stone bakehouse door behind the courtyard herb wall!
scenes.intro: Half past nine Saturday night in the warm glow of the front-desk lamp. As {F1}, {M2}, and {M1} turn through forty pages of joyful signatures in the Festival Guest Book, one crisp green-ink note on the final page catches {F1}'s eye. Listen first.
story: M2
Two hundred and twelve visitors signed our guest book today—my heart is completely full!
F1
Wait, {M2} and {M1}—read this last signature at the bottom of page forty!
M1
Green fountain ink and very neat block letters—who signed right before closing?
F1
Chief Editor, National Guide to Historic Inns—selecting {SHOW} for the new Annual Edition!
M2
A NATIONAL BOOK FEATURE?! Hold the counter, {M1}, my knees are wobbling again!
F1
Keep listening to the postscript underneath: Returning Friday with our photographer to see one marvel!
M1
Which marvel did the editor spot—Room Nine, the walnut piano, or the third stone?
F1
Listen: Especially curious about that low bricked stone arch stamped EIGHTEEN-NINETY behind your rosemary wall!
M2
A low stone arch stamped eighteen-ninety behind the courtyard herb shelves?!
M1
Hold on... behind that tall ivy trellis on the back wall sits an old iron ring!
F1
Wait—could that be the original wood-fired courtyard bakehouse mentioned on our brass plaque?!
M1
Fetch the lantern and my pruning shears—Season Four ends behind the ivy wall!
scenes.outro: {SHOW} holds the Golden Plaque, {F3} moves onto {STREET}, and behind the courtyard ivy waits a forgotten eighteen-ninety bakehouse arch! Season 4 of {SHOW} is complete—see you in Season 5!
